_about: Which redirect URIs an OAuth client may register and be sent to (RFC 6749 §3.1.2, RFC 8252 for native apps). The one description of it: the server embeds it (internal/oauthredirect) and the web app's consent page reads it (src/lib/oauth-redirects.ts), so the page follows exactly what the server accepts. https anywhere; http on a loopback host only, with any port at authorize and token time (RFC 8252 §7.3); a private-use scheme that is a reverse domain name (contains a dot, §7.1), or one of native_schemes; never a refused scheme, userinfo or a fragment. A private scheme can be claimed by another app on the device, so PKCE (S256) is required of every client.

native_schemes.cursor: Cursor registers cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback by DCR beside https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback and http://localhost:8787/callback, with no application_type (Cursor forum, 3.13.25 and 3.14.27).
native_schemes.vscode: VS Code's URI handler. VS Code registers https://vscode.dev/redirect (which hands off to vscode://) and loopback redirects (microsoft/vscode#278512); vscode:// admits a client that redirects to the handler directly.
native_schemes.vscode-insiders: VS Code Insiders' URI handler, behind https://insiders.vscode.dev/redirect, as vscode.
native_schemes.windsurf: Windsurf's URI handler (a VS Code fork). Its MCP OAuth redirect isn't publicly documented (checked Oct 2026); this admits its app scheme, as vscode.
